_what: Every system in sim/, the document section it implements, the roadmap task it belongs to, and the tests that prove it. The audit page reads this with status.json: a system is shown as built only if every test named here passed on the last run of status.py. A test that is renamed or deleted makes its system read 'missing', never 'built'.

systems.name: Fixed-point arithmetic
systems.what: 64-bit with 32 fractional bits for positions, 32-bit with 16 for angles. No floating point anywhere in the simulation.

systems.name: Angles and trigonometry
systems.what: Angles as a fraction of a turn, sine from a committed table computed in exact decimal arithmetic.

systems.name: Seeded randomness
systems.what: SplitMix64 into xoshiro256++, one stream per subsystem so one subsystem's draws cannot shift another's.

systems.name: The tick and its checksum
systems.what: Six phases in a fixed order; a checksum every tick, one a second kept, sensitive to one unit in the last place.

systems.name: Replay format
systems.what: Commands, never state. A header pinning 24.11's four things, a varint command log, and a four-byte checksum a second, under 2 KB.

systems.name: Golden replays
systems.what: Heists encoded by an earlier build and committed; every build re-simulates them and names the second any divergence starts at.

systems.name: Tile grid
systems.what: Per-tile terrain and continuous positions; 5.2's realm sizes; a fixed north-east-south-west neighbour order.

systems.name: Pathfinding
systems.what: Breadth-first, ties by tile index. Terrain slows the walk and cannot bend the route.

systems.name: Crew control
systems.what: The crew never makes a decision the player did not make: no re-routing, no different door, friends pass through one another.

systems.name: Line of sight
systems.what: Per tile, as 21.12 requires. Feet and eyes are separate properties, as 6.2's fence and fog bank require. The same line from either end.

systems.name: Noise
systems.what: Sound travels along the walkable path, never through walls: a guard turns toward the way around, not toward the source. The document's five carrying distances, in steps a crew would walk.

systems.name: Guard states
systems.what: Unaware, Suspicious, Investigating, Alerted, Searching, Returning, at the document's thresholds. No fall-back inside half a second; ten seconds searching the spot, twenty after losing sight, then home. Nothing random in it: §12.17 promises a scouting player can predict exactly what will happen.

systems.name: Realm alarm
systems.what: An alert reaches guards within four metres half a second later; the realm alarm climbs once every thirty seconds to six; at five one more Warden arrives at the entrance.

systems.name: Detection modifiers
systems.what: The corner of the eye at half the rate; crouched halves, running adds three quarters, an unlit tile halves again, multiplied once; still in tall grass is invisible until a guard walks into the tile; gravel and water carry sound further, moss less.

systems.name: Roles and gaits
systems.what: Crew and guards move at §11.1's speed for their role, over any number of tile edges. Walk, crouch or run by command; the two gait speeds are the simulation's reading, since the document gives neither.

systems.name: The Vault and loading
systems.what: 1,500 health a Vault level, cracked from beside it one hit every 0.8 s, Breakers for double; every hit is heard 5 m away. Once open, every crew member loads at 30 a second to the fill the player set, until the bag is full or the exposed share is gone — a full crew in ten seconds. A loaded Carrier walks 15% slower.

systems.name: Fights, knockouts and capture
systems.what: One hit every 0.8 s for Power, on both sides. An ambush on a guard that has not noticed the crew stuns it and two knock it out; an open hit sends it to 1000. A crew member at zero health drops its loot and is caught in ten seconds unless an ally revives it (3 s, a Mender 1.5). A knocked-out guard found by another raises the realm alarm.

systems.name: The skiff, the clock and the outcome
systems.what: The skiff comes to an edge tile in 20 s at the Heart and takes whoever holds the spot; anyone inside when the clock ends is caught. §12.9's four grades from who got out with what. A heist planned as a player would play it ends Clean with every bag full. Loading stops when the clock left no longer covers getting out; dropping loot costs exactly the fraction dropped.

systems.name: Laws and pylons
systems.what: All 48 laws as exact ratios, generated from content/law_effects.json. Each tick the rule sheet is the product of the laws whose pylons stand: speed, sight, suspicion, noise, structure and fight damage, alarm range, the clock, Glass and Stillness. A pylon broken — 600 health, Breakers double — switches its law off from the next tick and earns its page. A replay's rules field is a digest of the laws it was made under.
